title: Man. Post. Cap. V: open — quid sit imputari; Heb/Gk digression wasted
pass_a_gloss: CAPUT V examines Cap. III on what it is for sin to be imputed or not imputed. Having again laid down the state of the controversy in your third chapter, you digress once more and set yourself to explain imputare and imputari, first treating the Hebrew term and then the Greek, with several Scripture citations brought in for that purpose. I cannot tell to what end or plan you do this—unless it is to enlarge your tract and cloak how few arguments you actually have. That kind of illustration might help the justification debate, because Scripture often paints justification either by imputing faith and righteousness or by not imputing sin; but for the dispute between us I see no use in it, since Scripture nowhere says Adam's sin is imputed to us.
pass_b_english: CAPUT V. Examination of Cap. III, in which it is asked what it is for sin to be imputed or not imputed. In the third chapter you again set the state of the controversy, and once that is set you digress again, and take it upon yourself to illustrate what it is to impute and to be imputed, and you weigh first the Hebrew word, then the Greek, citing some places of Scripture to that end—to what purpose, or with what design, I do not know, unless perhaps so that you might swell the bulk of your treatise and cover the scantiness of your arguments. Useful enough, perhaps, your illustration would be for the controversy on justification—since Scripture is wont to describe that now by the imputation of faith and righteousness, now by the non-imputation of sin—but for this question which is between us I do not see what it is worth: for there is no place in all of Scripture in which Adam's sin is said to be imputed to us.
source_text: CAPUT V. Examen Cap. III. In quo disquiritur, Quid sit imputari vel non imputari peccatum. Capite tertio rursus constituis statum controversiae, eoque constituto iterum digrederis, ac tibi sumis illustrandum, quid sit imputare & imputari, ac primum verbum hebraeum, deinde verbum graecum expendis, laudatis in eum finem aliquot Scripturae locis: quorsum, aut quo consilio, nescio, nisi forte, ut tui tractatus molem augeres, ac tuorum argumentorum paucitatem tegeres: utilis quidem fortasse tua haec illustratio foret ad controversiam de justificatione: quoniam Scriptura eam solita est modo imputatione fidei & justitiae, modo non imputatione peccati describere: ad hanc vero, quae inter nos agitur, quaestionem quid valeat non video: Nullus enim extat in tota Scriptura locus, in quo peccatum Adami nobis imputari dicatur.
